answer: Use a synchronized bandwidth lottery. First, each identity commits to a public key before a random beacon fires. Second, every key must fetch a unique 2 GB challenge and return sampled hashes within 60 seconds. Third, validators reject reused data and late replies. Fourth, repeat at unpredictable times; a vine of fake accounts must feed every leaf at once. At a stipulated $0.01 per GB, 1,000 identities cost $20 per round and need 267 Gbps of ingress. Like jade caught in a karst fissure, one narrow passage stops a whole glittering hoard from slipping through.
